design:
Tier 2 (light). Hazard: the operator's :8000 Hub runs this slice's migration on its real database at the first restart after it lands. The migration adds three columns with defaults to slice 1's `dashboards` table and creates one table; it deletes and rewrites no existing row, existing dashboards becoming version 1. Rollback is its downgrade dropping the table and the columns, which loses only edit history, never a dashboard's name, description or panels.

Migration ordering: master's head is 0177_dashboards.py (slice 1, revision "0177"). The builder re-reads the head at build time (`git ls-tree master hub/hub/migrations/versions/`), names the file `NNNN_dashboards_edit_history.py` and points its down-revision at that head, re-checking before the last commit; it is guarded the way 0177 is (skip when already applied).

Decisions (operator-approved 2026-11-14 where marked, otherwise the author's):
- Edit in place, by operation: the edit names the dashboard, the version the agent read, and a list of operations. Slice 1's replace-whole save stays for creating, but a replace of an existing dashboard is also an edit: it takes an optional base version, bumps the version and keeps what it replaced, so it cannot bypass history or staleness.
- Every edit is validated like a save in slice 1 (panel shape and limits, chart kind in the fixed set, never-queryable boundary, project boundary, unique name; queries are not run), and applies whole or not at all. Panel ids are kept across edits; an added panel gets a new one.
- Each dashboard carries a version that goes up on every edit, replace or undo. A write naming an older version is refused with the current dashboard returned, never merged (operator, 2026-11-14).
- One kept version per dashboard; undo restores it as a new edit (operator, 2026-11-14).
- Repair needs no stored errors: agents get a run of a saved dashboard returning the same per-panel results the screen's run returns (dashboards.py:300-314, error and warning per panel).
- Ask to change (operator, 2026-11-14): the open dashboard offers a control that picks an agent, opens its conversation and fills the composer with 'Change the dashboard "<name>" (<id>): ', editable, sent only by the operator; nothing hidden is added to the turn. The look is mocked in hub/ui/mock route #tab/dashboards.

THE CONTRACT (bound to slice 1's shipped names: table `dashboards`, model Dashboard hub/hub/db/models.py:3719, ids `dash-<12 hex>`, panels `{id, title, query, kind}` with `id` `pnl-<12 hex>`, operator routes under `/api/v1/projects/{project_id}/dashboards`, agent routes under `/api/v1/agent-actions/dashboards`, tools save_dashboard / list_dashboards / read_dashboard / run_dashboard_query / dashboard_query_reference, events dashboard_saved / dashboard_deleted):

Columns added to `dashboards`: `version` Integer not null default 1; `edited_by` String(32) nullable (the agent from the run credential, or `operator`; never from the request body); `edited_at` UTCDateTime nullable.

Table `dashboard_versions` (model DashboardVersion), at most one row per dashboard: `dashboard_id` String(64) primary key; `project_id` String(64) FK projects.id, indexed (so ProjectLifecycle.delete's project_id sweep, hub/hub/project_lifecycle.py:432, reaches it with no code); `version`; `name`, `description`, `panels` as in `dashboards`; `edited_by`, `edited_at`. Every edit, replace and undo overwrites the row with what it replaced. The DELETE route deletes it explicitly.

Operations, elements of `operations`, each `{"op": ...}`:
- `{"op": "add_panel", "panel": {"title", "query", "kind"}, "position": int | null}` (null appends)
- `{"op": "remove_panel", "panel_id": str}`
- `{"op": "change_panel", "panel_id": str, "title"?: str, "query"?: str, "kind"?: str}` (only keys present change)
- `{"op": "move_panel", "panel_id": str, "position": int}`
- `{"op": "rename", "name": str}`
- `{"op": "set_description", "description": str}`

Routes (hub/hub/api/v1/dashboards.py):
- Agent: `PATCH /agent-actions/dashboards/{id}` body `{"base_version": int, "operations": [...]}` -> 200 view at version+1; `POST /agent-actions/dashboards/{id}/undo`; `GET /agent-actions/dashboards/{id}/run` -> slice 1's run result.
- Operator: `POST /projects/{pid}/dashboards/{id}/undo`.
- Refusals: 409 `{"detail": {"code": "stale_version", "message", "current": <view>}}`; 422 `{"detail": {"code": "operation_refused", "operation_index": int, "reason": "invalid_chart_kind" | "not_queryable" | "invalid_panel" | "unknown_panel", "message"}}`; 409 `dashboard_name_taken` for a rename; 409 `{"detail": {"code": "nothing_to_undo"}}`; 404 `dashboard_not_found` for another project's dashboard.
- Agent POST save (slice 1) and operator PUT take an optional `base_version`, checked like an edit's when present.
- The view (read, list summary, run, edit responses) gains `version`, `edited_by`, `edited_at`, `can_undo`.

Agent tools (hub/hub/mcp_server.py, `@_tool()`): `edit_dashboard(dashboard_id, base_version, operations)`, `undo_dashboard(dashboard_id)`, `run_dashboard(dashboard_id)`; `save_dashboard` gains `base_version`. Guidance: find the dashboard with list_dashboards by name or by the id the operator's message carries; on none, several or no name, ask which and call nothing that writes. All three new names join HUB_MCP_TOOLS in hub/hub/copilot_acp.py, and the tools/list snapshot test is updated.

Event: `dashboard_edited` `{"id", "name", "version"}`, broadcast after commit by edit, replace and undo, registered in hub/ui/src/hooks/useSSE.ts so an open screen refreshes.

UI: Undo on the open dashboard only when `can_undo`; edited-by line; Ask to change (agent picker -> conversation -> composer prefill); hooks in hub/ui/src/api/dashboards.ts invalidate `['project', projectId, 'dashboards']`.

CURRENT (slice 1): save(name, description, panels, dashboard_id?) -> whole replace; read; list; operator delete; operator run.
PROPOSED: edit(id, base_version, operations[]) -> version+1 | refused(reason, current); undo(id) -> version+1; agent run(id); replace keeps history and checks staleness.

open_questions.question: How deep is undo? Answer (operator, 2026-11-14): one previous version, one step of undo, and restoring is itself undoable.

How does the agent know which dashboard the operator means by 'this one'? Answer (operator, 2026-11-14): an Ask to change button on an open dashboard: pick an agent, its conversation opens with 'Change the dashboard "<name>" (<id>): ' in the composer, visible and editable; no hidden turn context.
On a stale edit, refuse or merge? Answer (operator, 2026-11-14): refuse and return the current dashboard.

problem: Slice first-dashboard shipped on 2026-11-13 (build-7b284fca6fb8). An agent can create a dashboard, or replace one whole: save_dashboard with a dashboard_id overwrites its name, description and panels (hub/hub/mcp_server.py:1001, hub/hub/api/v1/dashboards.py:416-429). Asked "add a panel for X", it has two bad choices: create a near-duplicate second dashboard, or rewrite the whole thing from memory and risk silently altering panels the operator liked. Nothing records who changed a dashboard, nothing keeps what a replace overwrote, and two edits from the same starting point silently overwrite each other. A panel that breaks (after a Hub upgrade, say) shows its error on the screen, but agents have no way to run a saved dashboard and see that error: the agent router has no run route (dashboards.py:39 router serves list, read, save and query only). This slice makes a saved dashboard something the operator keeps refining by asking.

requirements.rationale: A second near-duplicate dashboard per request is the failure the roadmap slice exists to remove.
requirements.statement: Asked to change an existing dashboard, an agent edits that saved dashboard: afterwards the project holds the same number of dashboards, the dashboard keeps its identity, and the Dashboards screen shows the change on the dashboard the operator already had.

requirements.rationale: Guessing between two dashboards edits the wrong one without anyone noticing.
requirements.statement: The agent edits the dashboard the operator means: the one named in the request, or the one the operator's Ask to change named; when the name matches no dashboard, or several, or no dashboard is named, the agent says so and asks which, and changes nothing and creates nothing.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-14: what the agent is told stays visible, rather than a hidden context the operator cannot see.
requirements.statement: An open dashboard on the Dashboards screen offers Ask to change: the operator picks an agent, that agent's conversation opens, and its composer holds an editable line naming the dashboard's name and identifier, sent only when the operator sends it.

requirements.rationale: The operator trusts a dashboard they have looked at; an edit that quietly rewrites other panels breaks that.
requirements.statement: An edit changes only what was asked: every panel, query, title, chart kind, panel id, the order of panels, the name and description that the request did not mention are unchanged after the edit.

requirements.rationale: A half-applied edit leaves a dashboard nobody asked for.
requirements.statement: The Hub applies an edit as a list of operations (add a panel, remove a panel, change a panel's title, query or chart kind, move a panel, rename or re-describe the dashboard); if any operation is refused, including a chart kind outside the fixed set, a panel that does not exist, or a name another dashboard of the project holds, no operation is applied and the refusal says which and why.

requirements.rationale: An agent works from what it read at the start of a long turn; the operator or another agent may have edited since.
requirements.statement: An edit or a whole replace made against a version of the dashboard that is no longer the current one is refused with a message saying the dashboard changed and the current dashboard, and nothing is overwritten.

requirements.rationale: Asking for changes is only safe if a wrong one costs one click.
requirements.statement: After an edit or a whole replace the Hub keeps the version it replaced, and the operator can restore it in one step from the Dashboards screen (and an agent can when asked); restoring is itself an edit, so it can be undone the same way; a dashboard with no earlier version offers nothing to restore.

requirements.rationale: Slice first-dashboard surfaces a broken panel but cannot mend it; this is the other half.
requirements.statement: An agent can run a saved dashboard and receive, for each panel, its result or its error and drawing warning, exactly as the screen shows them; asked to fix a broken panel, it can correct that panel's query from its error, check the new result, and change only that panel, after which the panel draws.

requirements.rationale: The edit path must not become a way round the query boundary.
requirements.statement: An edit's queries are held to the same limits as slice first-dashboard's saves (current project only, read-only, never-queryable data refused), and an agent cannot edit, undo, run or read the kept version of a dashboard belonging to another project.
Deleting a dashboard, or the project it belongs to, removes its kept earlier version.
The Dashboards screen shows who last edited the dashboard and when, beside the author and date.

in_scope: An agent tool to edit a saved dashboard in place by operations, with the version it read
Finding which dashboard the operator means: by name, or the one the operator asked about from the Dashboards screen
An Ask to change control on the Dashboards screen that starts the request in a conversation with the dashboard named
Refusing a stale edit and returning the current dashboard
Keeping the replaced version and one step of undo, on the Dashboards screen and for agents
An agent tool that runs a saved dashboard and returns each panel's result or error, so an agent can repair a panel by asking
Recording who last edited a dashboard and when, shown on the screen
non_goals: Full version history, browsing or diffing old versions (one previous version only)
Several agents or people editing at once with merging; a stale edit is refused, not merged
The operator editing panels by hand on the screen (changes are asked for)
A hidden 'open dashboard' identifier carried on the agent's turn; the dashboard is named in the visible message
Changing the query tool, the chart kinds, or the queryable data from slice 1
Fixing a panel's query automatically without being asked
Storing panels' last results or errors; a dashboard is run to learn them
Agents deleting dashboards (slice 1 keeps delete the operator's)
Sharing, exporting, or copying dashboards between projects

summary: The operator asks an agent to change a dashboard that already exists (add a panel, change a chart, fix a broken query). The agent finds the right saved dashboard, changes only what was asked in place, and the operator sees the same dashboard updated, not a new one. A change made on top of a newer edit is refused rather than overwriting it, the previous version is kept so one step undoes an edit, and a panel whose query broke is repaired by the agent from the error running it returns.
